title: Affine-target indeterminacy on a normal Noetherian integral scheme
statement:
Let $W$ be a nonempty integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] which is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact) and normal (every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]). Let $A$ be any commutative ring and let $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $D\subseteq W$ be a dense open subscheme and let $h:D\to H$ be a morphism. Define the open subset
$$E=\bigcup\{V\subseteq W\text{ open}:\ \exists h_V:V\to H,\quad h_V|_{V\cap D}=h|_{V\cap D}\}.$$
There is a unique morphism $h_E:E\to H$ restricting to every such $h_V$. Every irreducible component of the closed subset $W\setminus E$ has a generic point $\xi$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{W,\xi}=1$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The complement may be empty. No field, finite generation of $A$, or factoriality of $W$ is assumed.

source.place: BLR §4.4 Lemma 2, printed p.109 (PDF p.115). Supporting algebra: Stacks Tag 031T, algebra.tex, label lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1, part (2). Primary scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $\eta$ for the generic point of $W$ and $K=\mathcal O_{W,\eta}$. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], $\eta$ belongs to every nonempty open and sections on any such open inject into $K$. The affine adjunction [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] associates to $h$ a ring map $A\to\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_W)$, hence a map $\varphi:A\to K$. Every extension $h_V$ in the definition of $E$ induces the same generic map: if $V$ is nonempty then $V\cap D$ contains $\eta$. On each nonempty overlap $V\cap V'$, injectivity into $K$ makes their coordinate ring maps equal; the adjunction makes their morphisms equal. Empty overlaps have a unique morphism. Now [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives a unique $h_E$ restricting to all $h_V$. Since $D$ is one of these opens, $D\subseteq E$, and $h_E|_D=h$.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1 (2); affine-coordinate expansion of BLR §4.4 Lemma 2, printed p.109 (online scan PDF p.115).

proof.text: Put $Z=W\setminus E$. If $Z$ is empty there is nothing further to prove. Otherwise [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] writes $Z=C_1\cup\cdots\cup C_r$ as its distinct irreducible components. Fix one, $C=C_i$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] it has a generic point $\xi$. This point lies in none of the other $C_j$: membership would imply $C=\overline{\{\xi\}}\subseteq C_j$, contrary to maximality and distinctness. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $\xi$ inside $W\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j$. Thus $Z\cap U=C\cap U$. Write $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_W)$ and $\mathfrak p$ for the prime of $\xi$ under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$. On this chart $C\cap U=V(\mathfrak p)$, directly from the Zariski closure of a point. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $\mathcal O_{W,\xi}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1 (2); affine-coordinate expansion of BLR §4.4 Lemma 2, printed p.109 (online scan PDF p.115).

proof.text: The ring $R$ is a domain by integrality and is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Identify $\operatorname{Frac}R$ with $K$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. It is also integrally closed: for $a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}R$, $b\ne0$, integral over $R$, regard $a/b$ as the section on the principal open $D_U(b)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. This open contains $\eta$, so is dense in $U$. Apply [lem-sbc-normal-dense-open-integral-section] with ambient scheme $U$, dense open $D_U(b)$ and affine open $U$ itself. Its local normality and locally Noetherian hypotheses are inherited from $W$. It extends $a/b$ to $r\in R$; equality in $K$ gives $r=a/b$.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1 (2); affine-coordinate expansion of BLR §4.4 Lemma 2, printed p.109 (online scan PDF p.115).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-reflexive-height-one-intersection-criterion] to the $R$-module $M=R$. This is finite, torsion free, and reflexive: $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,R)\cong R$ sends $f$ to $f(1)$, with inverse $c\mapsto(r\mapsto rc)$; applying this twice identifies the bidual evaluation with the identity of $R$. The theorem therefore gives $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=1}R_{\mathfrak q}$ inside $K$, including the empty-intersection convention. This is precisely the scalar intersection assertion of Tag 031T(2), obtained from an existing more general node rather than introducing a duplicate.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1 (2); affine-coordinate expansion of BLR §4.4 Lemma 2, printed p.109 (online scan PDF p.115).

proof.text: The prime $\mathfrak p$ is nonzero: otherwise $\xi=\eta$, but $\eta\in D\subseteq E$ whereas $\xi\in Z$. Suppose some nonzero prime lies strictly below $\mathfrak p$. For every height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ of $R$ one then has $\mathfrak p\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$: inclusion would give a chain of at least two strict prime inclusions below $\mathfrak q$. Consequently its point $x_{\mathfrak q}$ does not belong to $V(\mathfrak p)=Z\cap U$, and lies in $E$. For every $a\in A$, the section $h_E^*(a)$ has a germ at $x_{\mathfrak q}$ whose image in $K$ is $\varphi(a)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], this means $\varphi(a)\in R_{\mathfrak q}$. Step 4 now gives $\varphi(a)\in R$ for every $a\in A$.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1 (2); affine-coordinate expansion of BLR §4.4 Lemma 2, printed p.109 (online scan PDF p.115).

proof.text: Because $R\hookrightarrow K$ is injective, the unique preimages of the elements $\varphi(a)$ define a unital ring homomorphism $\varphi_U:A\to R$: addition, multiplication and the unit can all be checked after this injection. By [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] it defines $h_U:U\to H$. On $U\cap D$, its coordinate maps and those of $h$ have the same generic germs $\varphi(a)$; injectivity from [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] and the affine adjunction show equality there. Hence $U$ occurs in the defining union for $E$, contradicting $\xi\in U\setminus E$. There is therefore no nonzero prime strictly below the nonzero $\mathfrak p$. The only chains of primes below $\mathfrak p$ have length at most one, and $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ has length one. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] and the stalk identification in step 2, $\dim\mathcal O_{W,\xi}=1$. This applies to every component of $Z$.

Step 3: R is a Noetherian domain with Frac R = K. R is integrally closed by lem-sbc-normal-dense-open-integral-section applied with X = U and the dense D(b), since O(D(b)) = R_b ⊂ K. Step 6: φ_U : A → R gives an h_U that agrees with h on U∩D, contradicting ξ ∉ E. So ht p = 1, and dim O_{W,ξ} = 1 by the chains-below-prime node. lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_affine_extension_and_indeterminacy_dim_one (W : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral W] [IsNoetherian W] (_hnormal : ∀ x : W, IsDomain (W.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (W.presheaf.stalk x)) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (D : W.Opens) (_hD : Dense (D : Set W)) (h : D.toScheme ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) (E : W.Opens) (_hE : E = sSup {V : W.Opens | ∃ hV : V.toScheme ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A), W.homOfLE (inf_le_left : V ⊓ D ≤ V) ≫ hV = W.homOfLE (inf_le_right : V ⊓ D ≤ D) ≫ h}) : (∃! hE : E.toScheme ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ∀ (V : W.Opens) (hV : V.toScheme ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)), W.homOfLE (inf_le_left : V ⊓ D ≤ V) ≫ hV = W.homOfLE (inf_le_right : V ⊓ D ≤ D) ≫ h → ∃ i : V ≤ E, W.homOfLE i ≫ hE = hV) ∧ ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents {x : W // x ∉ E}, ∃ ξ : W, IsGenericPoint ξ (Subtype.val '' C) ∧ ringKrullDim (W.presheaf.stalk ξ) = 1
